newsitem.title: CHINA: China congratulates Hong Kong's leader elect.
newsitem.headline: China congratulates Hong Kong's leader elect.

text.p: China congratulated Tung Chee-hwa on his election as Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive on Wednesday and urged Britain to offer him its help to ensure a smooth transfer of power next year.
"We congratulate the winner of the election," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told Reuters.
"It is our hope that the British side will offer due assistance to the chief executive so as to ensure the smooth handover and peaceful transition of the Hong Kong government," he said.
The 59-year-old shipping tycoon easily captured the lion's share of votes from a 400-member Selection Committee, making him the territory's leader-in-waiting.
The Selection Committee members were all hand-picked by China.
Tung will formally take up the job when Hong Kong returns to China on July 1, 1997, after 150 years of British rule.
"We believe that the newly elected chief executive will be able to lead the Hong Kong people to a more prosperous and stable Hong Kong," Shen said.
The spokesman, shrugging off suggestions that the poll was stage-managed by Beijing, said the elections were fair, open and democratic.
The official Xinhua news agency echoed that theme, saying in a commentary that the vote was an historic first for the territory and represented true democracy.
"It is not only an honour for him (Tung) but also reflects the wishes of the majority of Hong Kong compatriots," Xinhua said.
"It is China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong...that offers Hong Kong the unprecedented opportunity for its democratic development," the agency said.
